missing_spec_content.spec_text: The resistance of an LDR decreases as light intensity increases.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson never mentions LDRs. It has no statement of how LDR resistance changes with light intensity.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: The application of LDRs in circuits eg switching lights on when it gets dark is required.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson gives no application of an LDR in a circuit.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: The applications of thermistors in circuits eg a thermostat is required.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson only says 'A thermistor's resistance decreases as it gets hotter' (keyPoints[2].content). It gives no application such as a thermostat.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: The resistance of components such as lamps, diodes, thermistors and LDRs is not constant; it changes with the current through the component.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not state the general point that the resistance of these components changes with the current through them. LDRs are left out entirely.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: draw an appropriate circuit diagram using correct circuit symbols.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson has no circuit diagram and teaches no circuit symbols. Every diagram field is null. The required practicals also say 'use circuit diagrams to construct appropriate circuits'.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: relate the curves produced to their function and properties.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson explains the lamp and resistor curves. For the diode, it does not describe the forward-direction shape of the graph and links it to function only as 'one direction only'.

missing_spec_content.spec_text:
energy transferred = power × time

E = P t
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson teaches E = QV from this section but leaves out E = Pt. Students must recall and apply both equations ('Students should be able to recall and apply both equations').

missing_spec_content.spec_text: The amount of energy an appliance transfers depends on how long the appliance is switched on for and the power of the appliance.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not cover this.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to describe how different domestic appliances transfer energy from batteries or ac mains to the kinetic energy of electric motors or the energy of heating devices.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not cover energy transfers in domestic appliances. The intro only mentions a phone, a kettle and Christmas lights in passing.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to explain how the power of a circuit device is related to: the potential difference across it and the current through it; the energy transferred over a given time.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not mention power at all.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to describe, with examples, the relationship between the power ratings for domestic electrical appliances and the changes in stored energy when they are in use.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not cover power ratings.

above_gcse.text: The ions vibrate more and get in the way of electron flow
above_gcse.why: The specification sections given only require that the resistance of a filament lamp increases as temperature increases. The ion and electron model is not required by them. It is also repeated in checkpoints[3].wrongFeedback.

above_gcse.text: connected in series; has very low resistance / connected in parallel; has very high resistance
above_gcse.why: The resistances of the meters are not required by the specification sections given. This is minor and unlikely to confuse.

factual_errors.text: The resistance of a wire depends on its length and its temperature:
factual_errors.correction: The resistance of a wire also depends on its material and its cross-sectional area. As written, the sentence implies length and temperature are the only factors. The specification only asks for length at constant temperature in RP3.

not_checked: All diagram fields are null, so there are no circuit diagrams or I-V graph images to check. The shapes are only described in text.
